analysis.investment_thesis: KPI Green is a textbook fast grower riding India's 500 GW renewable energy mandate — revenue compounded at 93% over 6 years with net profit doubling in FY25 to ₹325 Cr, yet the stock trades at just P/E 20.6x, implying a PEG below 0.5 even on conservatively halved forward growth. At ₹448, you are paying a bargain price to own one of India's fastest-growing independent power producers in an industry with decades of visible tailwind.
key_strengths: Exceptional PEG <0.5 — P/E of 20.6 against ~60-70% recent earnings growth is the kind of mispricing Lynch hunts for
Operating margin expanding to 30.6% with EBITDA margin ~33%, proving pricing power as the company scales capacity
India's renewable build-out is a decade-long secular tailwind visible to any consumer — classic 'invest in what you know' thesis
key_risks: D/E of 0.88 breaches Lynch's 0.6 ceiling; borrowings surged to ₹2,533 Cr in FY25, raising refinancing risk if rates rise or growth stalls
Free cash flow was -₹1,297 Cr in FY25 — the company burns cash perpetually and depends on external capital to fund its own growth
Equity base quadrupled in one year (₹836 Cr → ₹2,650 Cr), signaling heavy dilution that can suppress per-share earnings growth even if aggregate profits rise
red_flags: CWIP jumped to ₹709 Cr and investing CF hit -₹1,587 Cr in FY25 — execution risk on massive capacity under construction
OCF was positive only 3 of last 5 years, unusual volatility for an asset-heavy utility
analysis.detailed_analysis: KPI Green is a rare find: a fast grower priced like a stalwart. Revenue surged from ₹34 Cr to ₹1,735 Cr in six years — a 93% CAGR — and net profit doubled from ₹162 Cr to ₹325 Cr in FY25 alone. Yet the P/E sits at 20.6x. Even if I slash the forward growth estimate to 30% to account for base-effect deceleration, the PEG is 0.69 — firmly in buy territory by my rules. ROCE of 17.5% and ROE of 19.7% show the capital deployed is productive, and operating margins are expanding, not contracting. The story here is blindingly simple: India is building renewable capacity at a wartime pace and KPI is one of the fastest-executing IPPs in the country. That's the kind of obvious tailwind I spotted with retailers in the 1980s.
